## The task

The block starts at rest on the floor and must end fully on the platform, at
rest. The disk alone cannot carry it. The **indirect lift** tips the block onto
the step corner, lets the disk walk round to the block's raised underside,
lifts the block off the floor and rolls it onto the platform, the block held at
every instant:

{g} → {m<sub>x</sub>, g} → {m<sub>x</sub>, g, s} ⇒ {m<sub>x</sub>,
g<sub>v</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>} → {g<sub>v</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>} →
{m<sub>z</sub>, g<sub>v</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>} → {m<sub>z</sub>,
s<sub>v</sub>} → {m<sub>z</sub>, t} → (transport) goal.

## 2026-11-19 … 11-21: the certified chain, the staircase, scene-generic learning {#latest}

Four lines of work. Every number below is from a committed record in
`RobotControlLab/certified-contact-graphs` (private); the commit or branch is
given with each. Anything not yet final is marked **pending**.

### The certified chain (issue #81, back half) {#the-certified-chain-issue-81-back-half}

The chain is one route of the lift built as certified funnels
([Certified funnels](../planar-build/funnels.qmd)): each edge certified for
every state of its entry set and every disk friction in [0.3, 0.5], each
junction a containment of certified sets. The junctions now need **real
margins**, and chain_check enforces them by default (ccg `a6161ffa5`):

- a link where the control switches holds by at least one measured one-step
  95/95 slack: the realized state's change over one step at the hand-off;
  for the rest links, the hold's own one-step change (decision 42 (a));
- a boundary between two certificates of one law, with no switch, holds by
  containment with a margin above the float32 forward-error bound of the
  compared quantity (decision 43 (a′)).

Every narrow link from the tip to the push passes (ccg `master` `eddbd2aa8`;
`ccg/scripts/edge_tube/results/i81/back/roll_push_entry/swap_after/cc_narrow.txt`):

| Link | Kind | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| tip departure → tip funnel | same-law boundary | pass |
| tip funnel → 23° switch → pivot | switch: slack | pass, ≥ 1 slack |
| pivot → stop at 59.00° | switch: slack | pass, ≥ 1 slack |
| stop at 59.00° → gentle break | rest: slack; force band | pass, ≥ 1 slack; force contained |
| gentle break + make(m<sub>z</sub>) | one certificate (a node, no junction) | — |
| make(m<sub>z</sub>) → tcbreak departure | rest: slack | pass, +1 slack |
| tcbreak departure → tcbreak funnel | same-law boundary | pass |
| tcbreak funnel → tcroll funnel (62°) | switch: slack | pass, ≥ 1 slack |
| tcroll funnel → push | switch: slack | pass, +1 slack (decision 54) |
| push → landing (impact window) | same-law boundary | **pending**: the cover is rebuilt |

The wide chain, from the post-impact rest set S<sub>rest</sub> through the
c3 departure, the wide funnel and the goal stop to the release, passes end
to end under enforcement (`CHAIN PASS (wide)`, ccg `c875eb515`,
`i81/back/goal_band_juno524821/cc_wide_band.txt`). S<sub>rest</sub>'s
independent holdout: 0 of 773 rollouts outside (Clopper–Pearson 0.39%; ccg
`c5354ee66`).

**Commanded forces over measured bands** (decision 44 (2)). Where a hold's
commanded force is handed from one certificate to the next, both
certificates are now certified over the command ± δ, δ the one-sided 95/95
bound on |realized − commanded| normal force at the hand-off, measured on
1,536 rollouts of the realizer (calibration half 768, held-out half 768):

| Junction | Command ± δ | Held out within δ | Record |
|---|---|---|---|
| stop at 59.00° → gentle break | 0.0311568 ± 1.07 × 10⁻⁴ N | 756 / 768 | `i81/slack/stop_force_break.json` |
| goal stop → release | 0.15 ± 0.00859 N | 757 / 768 | `i81/slack/rest_force_stop_release.json` |

At the goal stop the realized force lies one-sidedly above the command
(0.1574–0.1586 N at both ends of the friction band). Both certificates hold
over their bands (ccg `4313f9491`, `c875eb515`).

**The push, re-certified from the roll's grown exit** (decision 54). The
roll → push junction had compared the roll's exit with an entry the push
tubes never certified ([Issues](../planar-build/issues.qmd)). The push was
re-certified with the same law from the roll's exit grown by its slack: 16
of 16 sub-boxes hold, utilization 0.603–0.631, binding on progress (Juno
525614, ccg `13512e720`). Roll → push now passes at +1 slack.

**The same verdicts in float32.** Every re-certified piece was rerun in
float32 (fe32-poly) and holds with the same binding conditions: the lift
funnels, the roll junction and both departures (ccg `5e679b9a9`), the stop
(`8f15b80d4`), the goal stop and the release (`f7338e7b4`), and the
re-seeded push (utilization 0.598–0.626; `eddbd2aa8`).

**Pending: push → landing.** The landing's impact-window cover was certified
for the push's earlier exit; it is rebuilt from the re-certified exits (about
1,125 core-hours, measured on a smoke; ccg `fd271699a`) and is running on
Ganymede2.

### The staircase, with V₁ and π retrained on it {#staircase}

Branch `meas/staircase-v1pi` (`f226acf1c`), the **v0.3.1 stack** (not the
RSS headline's), on the 30 held-out starts (seed 13, starts 0–14, μ = 0.3
and 0.5) of the earlier V₀-only staircase measurement. V₁ and π are
retrained on the staircase (816 training searches, S_step's pipeline).

| Task | V₀ only | V₀ + V₁ + π | Gained / lost (exact McNemar) | Median calls to solve |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| first tread (P1) | 1 / 30 | **29 / 30** (83–99%) | +28 / −0 (p = 7.5 × 10⁻⁹) | 76 |
| top tread (P2) | 0 / 30 | **0 / 30** | +0 / −0 | — |
| S_step (control, S_step's own model) | 1 / 30 | 30 / 30 | +29 / −0 (p = 3.7 × 10⁻⁹) | 83 |

**Where the top tread stops.** All 30 searches land the block on P1 (first at
call 51, median) and reach the second lift's start, the block on P1 against
the second riser. There the gate offers V₀'s route edit, the tilt about P1's
edge, at 94 of the 97 such nodes, and π ranks it **last of four at all 94**
(median probability 0.001). No training search reached P2, so P2's goal
enters training only through hindsight goals.

**Held throughout** (the routes to the tread replayed as logged; both of
G3's criteria):

| Task | Ordering | Routes | Formation kept | Force in interval |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| first tread | V₀ only | 28 | 23 | 9 |
| first tread | V₀ + V₁ + π | 30 | 21 | 13 |
| route to P1 (top-tread task) | V₀ only | 30 | 24 | 10 |
| route to P1 (top-tread task) | V₀ + V₁ + π | 30 | 21 | 15 |
| S_step | V₀ only | 30 | 25 | 8 |
| S_step | V₀ + V₁ + π | 30 | 19 | 18 |

### Scene-generic V₁ and π (issue #86) {#scene-generic}

The goal: a value and ranker that transfer to new scenes without retraining.

**Step 1: S_step only** (branch `feat/scene-generic-v1`, `76c41cffb`). A
transformer over the scene's geometry as tokens (world frame, no positional
encoding), trained on S_step's 408 searches: 20 models (no augmentation,
Augerino, Laplace, untrained; 5 seeds each). It ranks S_step's held-out
searches as well as the current model (π top-1 95.2%, 95.1%, 92.6% against
93.4%; V₁ Spearman 0.916, 0.920, 0.873 against 0.927). As predicted, **no
variant learns the step-to-step symmetry** (invariant only if the P95 gap
is at most the P95 seed spread; V in calls):

| Variant | P95 gap / seed spread, step-to-step map |
|---|---|
| none | 7.45 / 3.52 |
| Laplace | 8.01 / 2.61 |
| Augerino | 6.19 / 2.34 |

Laplace's marginal likelihood collapsed every candidate augmentation; only
the far-field deletion (G6) collapsed as predicted, and the pre-registered
predictions for the other five candidates (G1–G5) missed. Augerino's continuous candidates
collapsed and its discrete ones went to their maximum, G6 included (a
miss). A hand-built symmetry also fails (4.94 / 2.14), so the bottleneck is
the staircase's unseen far field, not the frame. The misses are listed in
the branch's `ccg/scripts/learn/scene_generic/README.md`.

**Step 2: a pilot family** (branch `feat/scene-generic-m2`; in progress,
cutoff Nov 28).

- **The family.** 8 scenes drawn by Latin hypercube (seed 7830): 4
  staircases and 2 single steps for training, one of each for validation;
  the default staircase is held out. Validity tables and V₀ are built for
  all 8.
- **Round 0**: 450 searches (V₀ and the uniform ranker), launched on 11-21;
  results **pending**.
- **Global placement, pre-registered.** Round 1 runs each training scene at
  one random placement (seed 7915), so the learner can discover translation
  invariance from data; nothing imposes it.
- **The frame-local planner** (decision 56 (a′)). A placed scene's table and
  V₀ are computed in the scene's own frame, so they are exactly translation
  invariant: F1g1p's rebuilt table is identical to F1g1's in every field,
  where the world-frame build had differed in 28 of about 1,124 single edges.
- **A learned-canonicalization arm, pre-registered**: the same network on
  positions relative to a learned reference point (translation invariant by
  construction, labeled "architectural, not discovered"). It enters the
  online evaluation only if its 5-seed Laplace evidence separates from the
  world-frame model's.
- **At the cutoff.** If the pilot model solves the staircase's top tread
  zero-shot, it is RSS's lead learning result; otherwise RSS reports the
  top tread's 0 / 30 as the motivating limitation.

### Judge calibration for the RSS headline {#judge-calibration}

The judge ("held throughout", rule 3) compares each contact's measured stick
and slide per step against maxima. The maxima are recalibrated on the
headline's own realizer (decisions 45, 49, 50; branch
`fix/judge-recalibrate`, `3a1104f21`):

- **Population.** Fresh searches under the headline profile
  (`principled-noinform`) with the judge record-only (it records, it does not
  steer), from starts disjoint from the headline's (seed 7920), in batches of
  60; every fourth start is held out.
- **Thresholds.** For each (contact, quantity), the maximum over the
  calibration half's **successful** executions. A row needs n ≥ 59: the
  maximum of 59 samples is a 95/95 upper bound (0.95⁵⁹ < 0.05), and the
  held-out exceedance is about 1/(n + 1). A row with fewer than 59 has no
  threshold, and a call that needs one is unheld (decision 50).
- **Status after batches 1 and 2** (120 searches; 4 that crashed in the
  settle extension were rerun on its fix): 14 of 46 rows still have fewer
  than 59 (from m<sub>z</sub>'s slides, 52, down to the disk sliding on
  one block corner, 1); held out, 10 of 11,988 per-call checks exceed the calibration maximum.
  Batch 3 (60 more, 180 in all, the last under the stopping rule) is running.
  The final thresholds are **pending**.

## The planner finds it from the scene alone

The search is given the scene and the goal, nothing else: every edit the gate
admits except releases, transports toward the gate's targets, and outcome
children (a call's child is the state it reached). Each edit that places the
disk is offered at every placement along the face whose transition pose is a
distinct node under the search's own rule for identifying nodes. Every dynamic outcome is
rejected, so every solve is **held**. The motions are the quasi-static
realizer Λ<sub>qs</sub> in MuJoCo, with its contact rules on
([the local solver](../planar-build/local-solver.qmd#lambda-qs-options)). Both test sets are held out (never used
for training) and run at the band's two ends μ = 0.3 and 0.5, each search up
to 192 calls: 100 random lift starts (F1 seed 13), 200 searches; and the
original test set, the canonical start (the disk 10 cm from the block) and 16
random lift starts (F1 seed 11), 34 searches. The ordering is V₁ (round 2) and
the learned ranker π, trained on searches that offer every distinct placement,
with V₀'s measured edge lengths.

| Held-out set | μ = 0.3 | μ = 0.5 | All (Wilson 95%) | Calls to solve (mean / median) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 random starts (F1 seed 13) | 100 / 100 | 99 / 100 | **199 / 200** (99.5%; 97.2–99.9%) | 82 / 83 |
| Original: canonical + 16 (F1 seed 11) | 17 / 17 | 17 / 17 | **34 / 34** (100%; 90–100%) | 79 / 83 |

Every solve is held and is the indirect lift; 4 of the 199 hold the block by its
lower corner instead of its underside. The one failure among the 200 runs out
of actions to try. The canonical
start takes 86 calls at both μ (11 on the path).

**Every distinct placement against one placement per edit.** With the edit
offered only at the placement of largest margin and without the contact rules,
the same search (round 1 or round 2 of V₁ and π) solves 193 of 200 (94 and 99)
and 33 of 34. Paired on the same machines, every distinct placement with the
contact rules solves 6 searches of the 200 that one placement does not and
loses none (exact McNemar p = 0.031), and solves 1 more of the 34 (p = 1, run
on another processor). Where both solve, it needs 81 calls against 88 on
average. The two changes separate: without the contact rules, every distinct
placement gains the same 6 and loses 2, which reach the budget (p = 0.29); the
contact rules alone solve those 2 and lose none (p = 0.5), with the same calls
(81.5 on average). The 7 searches distinct placements gain each pass through
break s<sub>v</sub> at a further placement, a call that keeps the formation,
tilts the block further and is kept as a progress child.

**EULERDAMP off against on.** All these searches run with MuJoCo's EULERDAMP
flag disabled, so MJX integrates the solved acceleration. With it on, MJX
integrates a force sum that an unconverged contact solve can turn into a kick
of a block at rest. On the same machines, the one-placement searches with
EULERDAMP on solve 192 of 200 and 33 of 34 (193 and 33 with it off): 8 searches that fail with it on are solved
with it off, and 7 solved with it on fail with it off (exact McNemar p = 1).
Replayed call by call, three of the failures with EULERDAMP on come from such
a kick (one of them the first push, which flips the block upside down), two of
the solves with it on rely on the block's creep at rest failing a call, and
the others part at falls that end differently or at float-level differences
that grow along the search.

**Round 2 of V₁ and π**, trained on 408 searches (seeds 20–29), ranks better
offline (V₁'s Spearman correlation 0.87 → 0.93, π's top-1 84% → 94%) but
solves exactly the same searches as round 1: 193 of 200 and 33 of 34 on the
same machines (exact McNemar p = 1), with 88 calls to solve against 89, never
more, with one placement per edit. Its 7 failures among the 200 are exhausted
candidate sets, not ordering failures. (With EULERDAMP on, the same held: 192
and 192 of 200.) With every distinct placement offered, round 2's 280 searches
were run again (273 solved) and π retrained on the same 408; V₁ is round 2's.

**The configuration** (the defaults of `master`):

- transition poses must be admissible: no disk target buried in the block;
- transports aim inside their target sets by δ = 10 mm (the δ-erosion);
- the block's rotation range is ±180° (a ±90° joint stop could carry load);
- each approach is checked by the gate's hold test with the disk's own force, and refused before
  the disk moves if it would tip the block (the same 33 are solved with the same calls without it);
- unhinted search, dynamic outcomes rejected, 192 calls;
- EULERDAMP disabled: MJX integrates the solved acceleration;
- each disk-placed edit offered at every placement with a distinct transition pose;
- V₁ of round 2 and π retrained with every distinct placement offered, V₀ with edge lengths measured from logged calls.

**V₀** is the weighted graph distance to the goal plus a pose term
([how it is built](../planar-build/search.qmd#v0)); its edge lengths come from
the calls of round 0's training searches (a transfer succeeds 46% of the time, a
break 69%).
**V₁ and π** are learned by fitted value iteration and the LTS loss from
unhinted searches on other starts (F1 seeds 20–22, never the test set), in two
rounds: 80 searches of 64 calls, then 48 of 192 calls run with round 0's V₁ and
π. V₁ enters only the search's order; acceptance stays with V₀.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Another configuration (±90° rotation stop, admissible poses off)

Measured on the same 34 searches with the block's rotation stopped at ±90°, no
admissibility filter on transition poses, EULERDAMP on and, unless stated, no
δ-erosion. V₀
alone and round 0 were not re-measured in the configuration above.

| Ordering | Erosion | All | Calls to solve (mean) |
|---|---|---|---|
| V₀ + uniform ranker | no | 17 / 34 | 154 |
| V₁ + π, round 0 | no | 23 / 34 | 142 |
| V₁ + π, round 1 | no | 26 / 34 | 89 |
| V₁ + π, round 1, V₀ measured lengths | no | 28 / 34 | 88 |
| V₀ + uniform ranker | yes | 26 / 34 | 139 |
| V₁ + π, round 1 | yes | 33 / 34 | 87 |

In both settings the learned pair solves every search V₀ solves and more
(exact McNemar p = 0.004 without erosion, 0.016 with it), with 42–50% fewer
calls where both solve. Without erosion, of the 8 searches round 1 left
unsolved, 7 ran out of actions to try; with 64 calls none of 18 was solved: the
search reached {m<sub>z</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>} with the block at 51–57°, where
Λ<sub>qs</sub> refuses the roll, and the longer searches found a re-grip
(break m<sub>z</sub> to 63°, make m<sub>z</sub>).
:::

### Clips

Each clip replays the search's solution call by call on the processor that
ran the search (AMD EPYC 9334), and every call reproduces the log bit for bit
(43 of 43 calls). The clips come from the searches with every
distinct placement offered, with V₁ and π, run without the contact rules. With
them the canonical start at μ = 0.3 and start 1 take the same routes and calls;
the canonical start at μ = 0.5 goes by the lower corner (86 calls). The typical and lower-corner starts
are chosen by a script, not by hand: the most common route, then the search
closest to its median calls on the path and in the search.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How to read a clip

- **View.** From the side, with +x to the **left**, as in the paper. The
  green surface is the platform, the gray one the floor, the blue ball the
  disk. A red stripe marks the face the block rests on at the start.
- **Caption bar.** The run; the current edit *k/n* with its formations
  (σ → σ′); the call's outcome and the state it reached; the phase; the
  formation the recognizer reads right now; and whether the replay matched
  the log.
- **Speed.** The badge at the top left states it. The path plays as one
  motion: in real time while the block or the disk moves, easing to 3× while
  both rest. A call's outcome stays on screen while the next call plays.
- **Card.** The last frame carries the search's summary.
:::

2 mm ([issue #52](https://github.com/RobotControlLab/certified-contact-graphs/issues/52)).

## What this shows, and what it does not

- **The lift, found and held, at both ends of the friction band**, from the
  scene and the goal alone, on starts the learned parts never saw.
- **One scene, one task.** The step and the block; other scenes (the families)
  are not run.
- **Budget.** 3 of 200 searches (and none of 34) fail within 192 calls: two
  reach the budget and one runs out of actions to try.
- **The realizer.** Λ<sub>qs</sub> plans held poses, not stick–slip plans
  ([the local solver](../planar-build/local-solver.qmd#qs-slip)).

## Configuration and reproduction

The searches ran at certified-contact-graphs snapshot `ecb2d48c` with `--placement-distinct`, on
Juno's compute nodes; results, the jobs file and the comparison with one
placement per edit: `ccg/scripts/step4/chain_search/results/placement_distinct`.
V₀: `ccg/scripts/step4/value/results/v0_it1`. V₁ and π:
`ccg/scripts/step4/chain_search/results/placement_distinct/model_v1pi_pd`.
Under the recognizer's containment rule for endpoint-only contacts (`master`
`3b7954a4`, issue #53) all 234 searches are identical call for call
(`ccg/scripts/step4/chain_search/results/issue53`).
Searches run on CPU, one per 3 cores; a search needs about 80–90 thousand
memory mappings (`CCG_MAPGUARD` must allow them). All 234 searches ran on
Juno's compute nodes (AMD EPYC 9334, 262,144 mappings per process).
From `ccg/`:

```text
CCG_DISK_FRICTION=0.3 CCG_MAPGUARD=0 JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu PYTHONPATH=src .venv314/bin/python \
    scripts/step4/chain_search/run_chain.py OUT --no-hint --dynamic-outcomes reject --budget 192 \
    --v0 scripts/step4/value/results/v0_it1/v0_it1.json \
    --v1 scripts/step4/chain_search/results/placement_distinct/model_v1pi_pd \
    --learned-pi scripts/step4/chain_search/results/placement_distinct/model_v1pi_pd \
    --placement-distinct \
    --seed 11 --index 12
#   without --seed/--index: the canonical start; CCG_DISK_FRICTION=0.5: the band's other end
#   admissible transition poses, the delta-erosion and the approach check are on by default
```
